title: RAW UNREVIEWED: mineral Sol passes its properties through an intermediate liquid while the same coin persists
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Sloane73 c1460–70 explicitly distinguishes mineral Sol (natural gold) from the celestial Sun. Its complete florin recipe heats and quenches the same borrowed coin repeatedly in burning water or wine, pools replacement liquids if needed, then mixes that liquid into quintessence while forbidding direct quenching in quintessence. The coin remains almost the same weight. This is a scoped material-transfer alternative to astronomical action, not merely renaming Sun as gold.

source.work: The Book of Quinte Essence, F.J.Furnivall edition of Sloane73, EETS OS16
source.date: Sloane witness estimated1460–70 by E.A.Bond; edition1866, revised1889, reprint1965
source.span: BookI pp6–7, complete florin preparation; naming qualification pp2–3 and real solar heating alternative p6
source.source_layer: Public-domain editorial primary text, maintext column only; no new diplomatic manuscript collation. One witness, multiple local spans.

differentiating_relation: SOL_MATERIAL coin A persists across repeated HEAT/QUENCH(A,carrier B); B is then MIXED_INTO quintessence C; QUENCH(A,C) is expressly forbidden. A is still almost its former weight. The immediate preceding real-Sun alternative instead places a distillation vessel in summer solar radiation. Preserving A/B/C identity, action direction and negation scope cannot be accomplished by a global Sol-to-gold name swap alone.
complete_source_obligations: Borrow one good Florence florin; heat it on an iron plate but prevent iron itself touching the liquid.
Use glazed earthenware and the best available burning water; extinguish the fire promptly so the liquid does not waste.
Repeat fifty times or more; replace liquid only if too much is wasted, then combine all those liquids. This is not an instruction to use fresh water on every repetition.
The author claims the water retains the gold’s virtues and properties. Mix this treated water with quintessence; do not quench the florin directly in quintessence.
Best white wine is an alternative if burning water is unavailable. The florin remains as good and almost the same weight.
Claimed health/youth effects and the closing Sun-in-heaven analogy remain source content, not experimentally established chemistry or medicine.
known_counterexplanation: A direct-addition account collapses intermediate B into final C and violates the explicit prohibition. A complete-consumption account loses the persistent coin and its near-equal weight. An astronomical-influence account remains compatible with giving virtue in the abstract, but cannot literally supply the borrowed portable florin’s repeated liquid contact and weight relation. Merely assigning two senses to a target Sun-like form without compositional support remains underdetermined.

assumptions_and_limits: The source establishes SOL/gold polysemy and its operational consequences, not LUNA/silver in this particular complete recipe. OxfordTrinity9 Luna operations are catalogue leads only.
Nearly equal weight is not exact conservation, and a historical claim of extracted virtues is not a modern chemical result.
The warning for then it were lost leaves the pronoun referent unresolved; the direct-quench prohibition itself is explicit.
Real celestial and mineral Sun senses coexist in one witness and even one work; a global genre classification does not choose between them.
Q4 gold/silver separation is an additional complete local passage, but its words are gold/silver rather than Sol/Luna; no covert Latin equivalence is inserted.
Unconfirmed roles may support coherent exploratory readings; no requirement that a starting word be confirmed. No source resemblance authorizes arbitrary gloss assignment.
